This writ petition has been filed praying the following main reliefs:
"(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding and directing the opposite parties not to harass the petitioners in pursuance of false complaints moved by the Opposite Party No.4.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding and directing the concerned opposite parties not to interfere in the peaceful life and liberty of the petitioners.
Mansoor Ahmad @ Mohd.Mufeed Ahmad And ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin.Secy. Home And ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14618880/
1 (iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding and directing the concerned opposite parties to conduct fair and proper inquiry if any frivolous or false complaint is moved by the Opposite Party No.4."

The contention of the petitioners' counsel is that the opposite party no. 4 is filing repeated FIRs against petitioners only with the object of obtaining compensation/monetary relief under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and rules made thereunder in 1995 namely Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Rules, 1995.

Rules, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
He has invited our attention to Annexure-1, which is an FIR dated 10.7.2021, lodged by opposite party no. 4 against petitioner no. 2 alleging an offnece under Sections 376, 506 and 3(2)(5)
of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

In this case,
after investigation charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner no. 2.

Thereafter another FIR has been lodged by the opposite party no. 4 against both the petitioners, who are brothers, on 16.2.2022 alleging the offence under Sections 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Gha) and 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
On a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 16.2.2022, we find a recital that after getting their arrest stayed in connection with the first FIR referred above in a Crl. Misc. Writ Petition bearing No.
15592 of 2021, they were pressurizing her to enter into a compromise and in that process had committed the offence as alleged.

entities.text:
Crl. Misc. Writ Petition bearing No.
15592 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners thereafter has invited our attention to the third FIR dated 15.8.2023 lodged by the opposite party no. 4 against both the petitioners under Sections 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Gha) and 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, here again, the allegation interalia is of pressurizing the opposite party no. 4 to compromise in the earlier cases and in that process of having committed the offence as alleged.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The contention is that this is being done by her out of malice so as to harass the petitioners and also to obtain monetary relief meant for scheduled caste/scheduled tribes persons in such cases.
He says that the matter be got enquired by some higher Authority.

Learned AGA says that offences alleged against scheduled caste/scheduled tribes personnel are enquired by an Officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, therefore, whatever grievance the petitioners have they may raise it before the said Officer.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record, we cannot, at this stage, draw any conclusion as is being suggested by the petitioners, however, we leave this aspect to be considered by the Circle Officer concerned, who is Investigating Officer in the cases against the petitioners but say no more.
Let the petitioners approach the said Circle Officer in this regard or take such other action as may be permissible under law.
With these observations, the writ petition is disposed of but without prejudice to the rights of the informant in the pending investigation.
